summary.headline: TANFAC FY26 revenue hit a record INR711 crore (+27% YoY), but operating EBITDA fell to INR112 crore (16% margin vs 23%) on sulphur costs and a plant outage.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations reached a record INR193 crore, up 11% QoQ from INR173 crore in Q3. FY26 operating EBITDA fell INR17 crore YoY to INR112 crore and PAT fell INR18 crore to INR70 crore, with management attributing this to normalising margins after an exceptional FY25, higher sulphur prices, an HF plant outage and higher depreciation. The company is building a INR495 crore downstream project (INR405 crore for HFC-32 refrigerant gas) targeted for Q3 FY27, with about 65% of its 20,000 MTPA capacity reportedly contracted. Management was evasive on HFC-32 production quotas, which are yet to be allocated by the government.

+11% QoQ from INR173 crore in Q3 FY26

Down INR18 crore YoY from INR88 crore; margin down from 16%

financial_highlights.metric: Related-party revenue from parent Anupam Rasayan

segments.name: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) and sulphuric acid
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid plant ran at 101% capacity utilisation and HF plant at about 95% in FY26. About INR70 crore of HF output was lost to unplanned maintenance and a distillation column bottleneck in the old HF-1 plant, which is now at 100% capacity.

segments.name: Specialty fluorides
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 41% in FY26, and management expects it to improve as value-added product demand scales.

segments.name: Solar grade DHF
segments.commentary: Both phases were commissioned in FY26, taking capacity to 20,000 MTPA. Orders worth about INR1,068 crore run to about FY29, and the company says this books about 85% of capacity each year. Solar grade earns about INR15-20/kg more than merchant grade at a conversion cost of about INR3-5/kg.

guidance_outlook: Operating EBITDA margin from the existing business expected to stay in a 15% to 18% range.
HFC-32 plant (20,000 MTPA, INR495 crore total capex incl. INR405 crore for HFC-32 and INR90 crore for other products) targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27, with payback under four years.
Management expects HFC-32 revenue of about INR900-1,000 crore a year, and FY28 revenue of about INR1,600-2,000 crore; the INR3,000-3,500 crore aim is for five years.
Overall margin expected to stay in the same percentage range in FY27, with a 3-4% uplift from the final quarter of HFC-32 revenue.
A further 20,000 MTPA solar grade DHF plant and a 30,000 MTPA AHF plant are planned, to be announced in two to three months; target commissioning is around June 2027.
Next three to five years: INR500-700 crore of further investment, executed one project at a time.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is about 135,000 MTPA. HF capacity was doubled from 15,000 to about 30,000 MTPA in October 2024 for about INR100 crore.
Solar grade DHF capacity of 20,000 MTPA was fully commissioned in FY26 (two phases); the company claims it is the only Indian manufacturer and that it is below 10 ppb impurities.
HFC-32 plant of 20,000 MTPA at the Cuddalore site, about half complete, for commissioning around Q3 FY27 (Oct-Nov). Environment clearance and consent to establish are in hand.
Funding plan: about INR400 crore for HFC-32, of which INR100 crore from promoters via preferential allotment and about INR300 crore via QIP and term debt.

Long-term contracts cover about 65% of the 20,000 MTPA HFC-32 capacity (about 13,500 tonnes), with management aiming to sell a further 15-20%. Management says about 75-80% of that volume is export and 15-20% domestic.
demand_pricing: Management says India HFC-32 demand is about 22-23 KT and could roughly double to 45-50 KT in 4-5 years, driven by room AC growth of about 16-17% CAGR. Global HFC-32 demand is about 380 KT (2025), going to about 485 KT by 2030.

Indian merchant AHF demand is about 40 KT in total: solar about 15 KT, surface treatment 15-18 KT, specialty 10 KT. Solar capacity in India is expected to rise from about 36 GW to about 216 GW in five years.
Sulphur cost rose from about INR30/kg in FY25 to INR38-40/kg on average in FY26 and rose further in Q4. Pass-through to customers lags by about 30-45 days, and HFC-32 contracts are formula-based.
Q4 included a mark-to-market loss of INR2.5-3 crore from rupee depreciation.
Management says domestic methylene dichloride supply of about 425-430 KT exceeds demand of 310-320 KT, so chloromethane sourcing is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will the HFC-32 quota be allocated to TANFAC, and on what basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quota will be decided in 2027 by the government. It cited an office memorandum of 1 April 2026 and said the 2027 calendar year is free for production. Quota applies from 1 January 2028, and management declined to comment further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the break-even and cost of production for HFC-32?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated cost of production at about INR240-280/kg, including operating expenses, and said it was not in a position to give break-even utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR495 crore capex separate from the 30,000 MTPA AHF plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the AHF plant is not included. It will be announced in the next two to three months, and the company expects to start it about four months later, with the solar grade expansion running alongside.

qa_highlights.question: What penalties apply if HFC-32 supply is missed because of quota non-allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no penalty for quota-related non-supply. Penalties are mutual and apply only once production starts. Management did not quantify any contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a strong, unusual Q3 FY25, sulphur prices rising from about INR30/kg to INR38-40/kg, a Q4 M2M loss of INR2.5-3 crore, about INR70 crore of HF output lost to an outage, and INR7 crore of extra depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR400 crore will be raised: INR100 crore from promoters via preferential allotment and about INR300 crore via QIP and term debt. Beyond that, funding depends on accruals and market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any overlap with parent Anupam Rasayan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product lists are fully distinct, with no overlap in fluorine downstream or other products.

risks_watch: HFC-32 quota allocation is unresolved. Management would not address questions on whether the government will allocate quota to new entrants, and an analyst raised doubts about incumbents absorbing the Kigali-permitted volume.

Contract enforceability: the HFC-32 contracts depend on quota and are not yet in production. Management said there is no penalty for quota-related non-supply. Contract values, customer names and margins were not disclosed.
Sulphur and fluorspar input costs are rising, and pass-through lags by about 30-45 days. Management says the margin will remain in the same range.
Specialty fluoride utilisation of about 41% and the ramp of solar grade DHF should be tracked.
Funding: the INR300 crore QIP and term debt, and the timing of the INR100 crore promoter preferential issue, are not yet confirmed.
Track the Q3 FY27 HFC-32 commissioning date and the announcement of the AHF and solar grade expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, order visibility and execution, but defensive and evasive on HFC-32 quota risk: management repeatedly referred analysts to the government office memorandum. It was also reticent on contract margins and customer names, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We are going ahead with our plant of 20,000 metric tons and we are halfway through it and our capacity will be commissioned probably in October end or November, early November, Q3 of FY27.
So there is no penalty clause due to this or anything.
So the demand is going to grow almost to four-five folds, six folds.
